# P11 — Ruth 4:1-8

## 1. Metadata
- **Pericope title:** The gate: the non-name, the field before Ruth, and the sandal
- **BCV:** Ruth 4:1-8
- **Genre Group:** NARRATIVE
- **Genre:** HISTORICAL_NARRATIVE
- **Register:** INFORMAL_CASUAL

*(Versification note: Ruth's chapter and verse numbers are the same in English and Hebrew — no divergence in this pericope.)*

**Multi-level register tagging:**
The whole passage sits in INFORMAL_CASUAL. Scenes 2 through 4 shift to FORMAL_OFFICIAL at scene level: from the moment the ten elders are seated, the talk is a legal proceeding at the town gate — offer, terms, refusal, and the attestation act, all spoken before witnesses. Scene 1 stays in the plain narrative key: the convening — Boaz sitting down, the redeemer passing, "turn aside, sit here" — is brisk, not yet the proceeding. The narrator's aside at v.7, explaining the old custom to the listeners, stays the narrator's own plain voice inside the formal scene.

## 2. Level 1 — Whole-Passage Movement

### 2.1 Prose Arc / Shape / Argument / Burden / Concern
The passage is the day Naomi spoke of: the man does not rest. Boaz goes up to the gate and sits down — and behold, the redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken is passing by. Boaz calls him to turn aside and sit, calling him So-and-so, without a name, and seats ten men of the town's elders. Then the matter. First the field alone: the portion of our brother Elimelech, which Naomi, back from the fields of Moab, is selling — buy it before those seated and before the elders of my people; if you will redeem, redeem; if you will not, tell me, for there is no one besides you to redeem, and I am after you. The man says: I will redeem. Then Boaz adds: on the day you buy the field from Naomi's hand, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. And the redeemer turns back: I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance — you redeem my right of redemption, for I cannot redeem. The narrator pauses to explain the old way in Israel — for redeeming and for exchanging, to confirm every matter, a man drew off his sandal and gave it to his fellow; this was the attestation. So the redeemer says to Boaz, buy it for yourself — and draws off his sandal. What weighs on the passage is the order of the telling: Boaz speaks first of the field alone, and the man says I will redeem; then he says that whoever buys the field also acquires Ruth, and the man says I cannot. The narrator does not say why Boaz speaks in this order.

### 2.2 Context
This is the scene Naomi's word from that morning pointed to — the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today (3:18). Boaz sits down at the gate, and behold, the redeemer of whom he had spoken passes by; the narrator does not say why he passes at that moment. The nearer redeemer Boaz disclosed in the dark (3:12) now sits in daylight, and the narrator does not give his name: Boaz calls him peloni almoni — So-and-so, a way of speaking of someone without saying his name — and the narrator calls him only "the redeemer". Naomi's selling of Elimelech's portion is the first the audience hears of a field to sell. Ruth is named "the Moabite, the wife of the dead": her husband still goes unnamed. Through all eight verses Ruth and Naomi are not at the gate, and neither of them speaks; at the gate no one speaks of the night at the threshing floor; and no one says the name of God.

### 2.3 Emotion / Tone / Pace
Brisk, public, and procedural — the opposite key from the night before. The scene moves in quick commands: turn aside, sit here, sit here. The offer is business-like, the first answer confident — I will redeem. Then one verse from Boaz — on the day you buy the field you also acquire Ruth — and the answer turns into I cannot, said twice. The narrator's aside about the old custom slows the scene before its one physical act; the sandal comes off in full view.

### 2.4 Communicative Function
This passage settles the matter Boaz bound to the order of redeemers at 3:12–13: there is no one besides the nearer man to redeem, and Boaz is after him (4:4); the nearer man says he cannot redeem, and the right of redemption passes to Boaz, with a sandal for the attestation. It keeps the order of the telling — the field first, then Ruth — and the man's two answers. It leaves the nearer redeemer unnamed while Ruth is named again as the Moabite. It speaks of raising up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. Ruth and Naomi stay offstage, no one at the gate speaks of the night, and the name of God is not spoken. And it explains the sandal custom to the listeners, as a thing of former times in Israel. To speak this passage is to keep the procedure's plainness, the order of the telling and the man's two answers, the non-name, and the silences: the women, the night, and the name of God.

## 3. Level 2 — Scenes / Episodes

### Scene 1 — The gate convened: the passer-by and the ten (4:1–2)

**3A — Beings**

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז / Boaz
- Role: the convener — he goes up to the gate, calls the redeemer aside, and seats the elders
- Relationship: the redeemer who promised under oath at 3:13 to redeem if the nearer redeemer would not
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B19-The-Nearer-Redeemer]] — פְּלֹנִי אַלְמֹנִי / "So-and-so"
- Role: the nearer redeemer, called from his road to sit
- Relationship: kinsman of [[B2-Elimelech]] Elimelech's line; a redeemer nearer than Boaz, who comes first because he is nearer (3:12)
- Referential form: Boaz calls him peloni almoni — So-and-so, without a name; the narrator calls him only "the redeemer"
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B20-Elders]] — עֲשָׂרָה אֲנָשִׁים מִזִּקְנֵי הָעִיר / "ten men of the elders of the town"
- Role: the seated witnesses who make the gate a court
- Relationship: the town's elders, convened by Boaz
- Presence: PRESENT

**3B — Places**

[[PL7-Gate]] — הַשַּׁעַר / the gate
- Role: the venue — where the town's business is done and witnessed
- Type: the town gate, the public meeting-and-law place
- Effect on scene: the gate is where the matter is done before everyone

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0006-Gate-Legal-Venue]] — הַשַּׁעַר / the gate
- What it is: the gate as the town's legal venue — where what is done is done before everyone
- Function in scene: the place where Boaz sits down; the place where the matter is settled before witnesses

[[CB_0001-Kinsman-Redeemer]] — הַגֹּאֵל / "the redeemer"
- What it is: the redeemer's duty
- Function in scene: the narrator's only name for the passer-by — the role walks in before any terms are spoken

[[CB_0045-Nearer-Redeemer]] — הַגֹּאֵל … אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר־בֹּעַז / "the redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken"
- What it is: the redeemer nearer than Boaz, who comes first because he is nearer
- Function in scene: the redeemer Boaz spoke of at 3:12; he answers first

**3D — Times**
- None as a distinct frame: the scene opens the day Naomi named — "the man will not rest unless he has finished the matter today".

**3E — What Happens**
[[B13-Boaz]] Boaz goes up to the [[PL7-Gate]] gate and sits down — and behold, the redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken is passing by. Boaz says: turn aside, sit here, So-and-so — and he turns aside and sits. Boaz takes ten men of the town's elders and says: sit here — and they sit.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Convenes the court: Boaz sits, the redeemer sits, the ten elders sit. The redeemer is passing just then, and the narrator does not say why.

**Significant Absence**
The narrator does not give his name; Boaz calls him So-and-so. The narrator does not say why he passes at that moment. Ruth and Naomi are not present, and will not be, through the whole proceeding.

### Scene 2 — The first stage: the field, and "I will redeem" (4:3–4)

**3A — Beings**

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז / Boaz
- Role: the one who lays out the field-matter before the court
- Relationship: a redeemer of the line; after the nearer redeemer — "I am after you" (4:4)
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B19-The-Nearer-Redeemer]] — הַגֹּאֵל / "the redeemer"
- Role: the one given first right — and who takes it: I will redeem
- Relationship: the nearer redeemer
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B20-Elders]] — זִקְנֵי עַמִּי / "the elders of my people"
- Role: the witnesses the buying is to happen before
- Relationship: the seated court
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B3-Naomi]] — נָעֳמִי הַשָּׁבָה מִשְּׂדֵה מוֹאָב / "Naomi, who returned from the fields of Moab"
- Role: the seller — the widow whose hand holds Elimelech's portion
- Relationship: widow of [[B2-Elimelech]] Elimelech; mother-in-law of Ruth; absent from the scene
- Referential form: named with her whole story — "who returned from the fields of Moab"
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B2-Elimelech]] — אָחִינוּ אֱלִימֶלֶךְ / "our brother Elimelech"
- Role: the dead man whose portion is the matter
- Relationship: the dead husband and father whose line the redeeming serves; "our brother" — kin to both men at the gate
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

[[PL7-Gate]] — implied
- Role: the court in session
- Type: the town gate
- Effect on scene: every word of the offer is public

[[PL5_ELIMELECH_PORTION-Elimelechs-Portion-of-the-Field]] — חֶלְקַת הַשָּׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר לְאָחִינוּ לֶאֱלִימֶלֶךְ / "the portion of the field that was our brother Elimelech's"
- Role: the matter itself — the family land to be redeemed
- Type: an owned field-portion of the dead man's line
- Effect on scene: the family land, spoken of here for the first time

[[PL2-Fields-of-Moab]] — שְּׂדֵה מוֹאָב / "the fields of Moab"
- Role: where Naomi returned from — her identifying story
- Type: the country of the sojourn and the deaths
- Effect on scene: carries the book's whole first act inside the seller's name

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0003-Inheritance]] — the field-portion at stake
- What it is: the family landholding — the inheritance that keeps a line's name on the ground
- Function in scene: what Naomi is selling and what the redeemer is asked to buy back into the family


**3D — Times**
- None: continuous within the convened session.

**3E — What Happens**
[[B13-Boaz]] Boaz says to the redeemer: the portion of the field that was our brother [[B2-Elimelech]] Elimelech's — [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi, who returned from the fields of Moab, is selling it. And I said: I will uncover your ear — I resolved to tell you — buy it before those seated and before the elders of my people. If you will redeem, redeem; and if you will not redeem, tell me, that I may know — for there is no one besides you to redeem, and I am after you. And he says: I will redeem.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Lays the field alone before the court, and the redeemer says: I will redeem.

**Significant Absence**
Ruth is not mentioned in this first offer; Boaz speaks of the field alone. How Naomi came to hold the right to sell, and why this is the first the audience hears of a field, the narrator never explains. The dead man is "our brother"; his sons are not named.

### Scene 3 — The second stage: Ruth named, and the decline (4:5–6)

**3A — Beings**

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז / Boaz
- Role: the one who adds the second term — on the day you buy the field, you also acquire Ruth
- Relationship: the redeemer after this man, if he does not redeem (4:4)
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B19-The-Nearer-Redeemer]] — הַגֹּאֵל / "the redeemer"
- Role: the one who reverses — I cannot redeem, lest I ruin my own inheritance
- Relationship: the nearer redeemer, now declining
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B9-Ruth]] — רוּת הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּה אֵשֶׁת־הַמֵּת / "Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead"
- Role: acquired with the field, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance
- Relationship: widow of the unnamed dead son; daughter-in-law of [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi; absent from the scene
- Referential form: "the Moabite" and "the wife of the dead" — the foreigner-marker, spoken by Boaz in the terms; her husband still unnamed
- Presence: REFERENCED

[[B3-Naomi]] — מִיַּד נָעֳמִי / "from the hand of Naomi"
- Role: the hand the field is bought from
- Relationship: the seller; absent
- Presence: REFERENCED

The dead — הַמֵּת / "the dead"
- Role: the one whose name must be raised upon his inheritance
- Relationship: Ruth's late husband; his name is not said here
- Presence: REFERENCED

**3B — Places**

[[PL7-Gate]] — implied
- Role: the court in session
- Type: the town gate
- Effect on scene: the reversal happens in front of every witness

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[CB_0005-Name-Preservation]] — שֵׁם־הַמֵּת / "the name of the dead"
- What it is: the dead man's name as a thing to be kept alive on his land
- Function in scene: the stated purpose of acquiring Ruth: to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance

[[CB_0002-Widow-Acquired-to-Raise-Up-the-Name-of-the-Dead]] — לְהָקִים שֵׁם־הַמֵּת עַל־נַחֲלָתוֹ / "to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance"
- What it is: the widow acquired with the field, so that the name of the dead is raised up upon his inheritance
- Function in scene: what Boaz says acquiring Ruth is for; the term the nearer redeemer says he cannot take on

[[CB_0039-Living-and-Dead-Formula]] — הַמֵּת / "the dead"
- What it is: the dead man kept in the family's reckoning: "the dead"
- Function in scene: the dead man has a name and an inheritance; the terms are for raising up his name

[[CB_0003-Inheritance]] — נַחֲלָתוֹ / נַחֲלָתִי / "his inheritance … my inheritance"
- What it is: the landholding that carries a name
- Function in scene: set side by side: Boaz's "to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance" and the man's "lest I ruin my own inheritance"; he does not explain how it would ruin his own

[[CB_0004-Moabite-Outsider]] — הַמּוֹאֲבִיָּה / "the Moabite"
- What it is: the foreigner-marker
- Function in scene: the foreigner-marker, spoken by Boaz in the terms

**3D — Times**

[[TM_DAY_OF_PURCHASE-Day-of-Purchase]] — בְּיוֹם־קְנוֹתְךָ / "on the day you buy"
- What it is: the buying-day as the terms' time
- Function: a content-time inside the offer — the acquiring of Ruth falls on the same day as the field; the scene itself runs on in the session

**3E — What Happens**
[[B13-Boaz]] Boaz says: on the day you buy the field from the hand of [[B3-Naomi]] Naomi, you also acquire [[B9-Ruth]] Ruth the Moabite, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance. And the redeemer says: I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I ruin my own inheritance. You — redeem my right of redemption for yourself, for I cannot redeem.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Boaz adds the second term — whoever buys the field also acquires Ruth, to raise up the name of the dead — and the man who said I will redeem now says I cannot, and gives his right of redemption to Boaz.

**Significant Absence**
Why it would ruin the man's inheritance is never explained; he says only "I cannot", twice. Ruth and Naomi are not at the gate; neither of them speaks. At the gate no one speaks of the night at the threshing floor. The dead husband is "the dead"; his name is not said here.

### Scene 4 — The custom told, and the sandal drawn (4:7–8)

**3A — Beings**

[[B19-The-Nearer-Redeemer]] — הַגֹּאֵל / "the redeemer"
- Role: the one who confirms — buy it for yourself — and draws off his sandal
- Relationship: the nearer redeemer, withdrawing by the old form
- Presence: PRESENT

[[B13-Boaz]] — בֹּעַז / Boaz
- Role: the one the right of redemption passes to
- Relationship: the redeemer who now holds the right of redemption
- Presence: PRESENT

**3B — Places**

[[PL7-Gate]] — implied
- Role: the court where the act is done in view
- Type: the town gate
- Effect on scene: the attestation is done before everyone

[[PL_ISRAEL-Israel]] — בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל / "in Israel"
- Role: the realm the custom belonged to, in the narrator's aside
- Type: the people-land of the old way
- Effect on scene: sets the act inside a remembered, shared custom

**3C — Objects and Concepts**

[[O26-Sandal]] — נַעֲלוֹ / "his sandal"
- What it is: the sandal drawn off
- Function in scene: the sign that confirmed the matter (4:7); by the custom the narrator has just told, a man gave his sandal to the other

[[CB_0007-Attestation-Custom]] — הַתְּעוּדָה / "the attestation"
- What it is: the old confirming-custom — for redeeming and for exchanging, a man drew off his sandal and gave it to his fellow
- Function in scene: the narrator's explanation of what the audience is about to see, told as a thing from former times

**3D — Times**

[[TM_FORMER_TIMES-In-Former-Times-in-Israel]] — לְפָנִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל / "formerly in Israel"
- What it is: the narrator's time-marker for the custom — the former days
- Function: frames the aside, not the scene: the act happens now; the explanation reaches back

**3E — What Happens**
Now this was formerly in Israel, for the redeeming and for the exchanging, to confirm every matter: a man drew off his sandal and gave it to his fellow — this was the attestation in Israel. So [[B19-The-Nearer-Redeemer]] the redeemer says to [[B13-Boaz]] Boaz: buy it for yourself — and he draws off his sandal.

**3F — Communicative Purpose**
Closes the proceeding with its one physical act. First the narrator stops to explain the old custom; then the sandal comes off: the right is Boaz's, attested in the old form.

**Significant Absence**
No words of parting are given to the nearer redeemer. The terms now Boaz's — the field, the widow, the name — are not restated. In the whole proceeding no one says the name of God.
